title: Limb Injuries: PCP Assessment, Pain Relief and Splinting
next: Chapter 28, Lesson 2: Pelvis, hip and femur injuries, dislocations, and complications

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already splint, check distal pulses, apply cold and coach inhaled pain relief. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Use the mechanism to predict injuries, including the hidden ones
  2. Run a full PCP limb exam: the 6 Ps and a one-minute nerve check
  3. Sharper pain-relief and splinting choices, incl. BC traction

Textbook: Chapter 28, PDF pages 2277–2361
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you've all splinted fractures, checked pulses below an injury, put on cold packs, and coached patients through Entonox. So today isn't about how to tie a splint. It's about thinking like a PCP. First, we'll use the mechanism of injury to predict what's broken, including injuries that hide behind the obvious one. Second, we'll do a deeper limb exam: the six Ps and a one-minute nerve check. Third, we'll make sharper decisions about pain relief and splinting, ending with the BC traction splint. These injuries rarely kill, but they often disable, so good decisions on scene really matter.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们都给骨折上过夹板、查过伤处远端的脉搏、敷过冷袋，也指导过病人吸 Entonox。所以今天不讲夹板怎么绑，而是讲怎么像 PCP 一样思考。第一，用受伤机制推测哪里断了，包括藏在明显伤后面的伤。第二，做更深入的肢体检查：6P 和一分钟神经检查。第三，在镇痛和夹板上做更精准的决定，最后讲 BC 的牵引夹板。这类伤很少致命，却常常致残，所以现场的决定真的很重要。

slides.title: The whole patient before the limb
slides.body:
A fracture can wait. The airway can't.

70–80% of multisystem trauma patients have a bone or joint injury.

FracturePossible hidden blood loss
Pelvis1,500–3,000 mL
Femur1,000–1,500 mL
Humerus, tibia/fibula, elbow, ankle250–500 mL
Radius or ulna150–250 mL
slides.say: Before you look at any limb, remember the order. Seventy to eighty percent of patients with multisystem trauma have at least one bone or joint injury, and a twisted leg grabs everyone's attention. But a fracture can wait; the airway can't. Do your primary survey first. Then think about blood. Broken bones bleed into the tissues, where you can't see it. A pelvic fracture can hide one and a half to three litres, and a femur one to one and a half litres, so add the fractures together. As a PCP, these numbers tell you when a limb injury has become a circulation problem.
slides.sayZh: 看任何肢体之前，先记住顺序。多系统创伤的病人里，百分之七十到八十至少有一处骨或关节损伤，一条扭曲的腿会吸引所有人的注意。但骨折可以等，气道不能等。先做初检。然后想到血：骨折会往组织里出血，你看不见。骨盆骨折可以藏一点五到三升血，股骨一到一点五升，所以多处骨折要加起来算。作为 PCP，这些数字告诉你，什么时候肢体伤已经变成了循环问题。

slides.title: Mechanism predicts the injury
slides.body:
• Direct blow: the bone breaks where it is hit
  • Indirect: force travels along the bone (knee on dashboard → hip)
  • Fall on an outstretched hand: wrist, elbow, shoulder, collarbone
  • Twisting: spiral fractures, torn ligaments
  • Fatigue (repeated stress); pathologic (bone weakened by disease)
  • Landing on the heels: check knees, hips, pelvis and spine

Paired bones and rings (radius–ulna, tibia–fibula, pelvis) often break in two places.
slides.say: The mechanism is your best predictor. A direct blow usually breaks the bone right where it lands. An indirect force travels along the bone and breaks something further away; a knee hitting the dashboard can drive the femur back and injure the hip. A fall on an outstretched hand can hurt the wrist, elbow, shoulder or collarbone. Twisting causes spiral fractures and torn ligaments. Fatigue fractures come from repeated stress, and pathologic fractures happen in bone weakened by disease, such as cancer. Landing on the heels can also injure the knees, hips, pelvis and spine. And paired bones and rings rarely break in only one place.
slides.sayZh: 受伤机制是你最好的预测工具。直接暴力通常在着力点把骨头打断。间接暴力沿着骨头传导，把更远的地方弄断：膝盖撞到仪表盘，可以把股骨往后推，伤到髋部。伸手撑地摔倒可以伤到手腕、肘、肩或锁骨。扭转造成螺旋形骨折和韧带撕裂。疲劳骨折来自反复应力；病理性骨折发生在被疾病削弱的骨头上，比如癌症。双脚跟着地还可能伤到膝、髋、骨盆和脊柱。还有，成对的骨和环形结构很少只断一处。

slides.title: Fracture, dislocation, sprain or strain?
slides.body:
InjuryWhat is hurtTypical clue
Fracturebonedeformity, point tenderness
Dislocationjoint surfaces fully apartjoint locked, severe pain
Sprainligament (bone to bone)swelling, usually no deformity
Strainmuscle or tendonpain on stretch, bruising later

Any wound near a fracture = open fracture. With a dislocation or severe sprain, assume a fracture too.
slides.say: On scene you'll sort limb injuries into four groups. A fracture is a break in the bone. In a dislocation, the joint surfaces have separated completely; muscle spasm locks the joint, so it barely moves and it hurts a lot. A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament, the band joining bone to bone, usually with no deformity. A strain is an injury to a muscle or tendon. Two safety rules. Any wound near a fracture makes it an open fracture, even with no bone showing, because the bone end may have poked out and slipped back. And your hands can't rule out a fracture, so treat a dislocation or severe sprain as if one is there.
slides.sayZh: 现场可以把肢体伤分成四类。骨折是骨头断了。脱位是关节面完全分开，肌肉痉挛把关节锁住，所以几乎动不了，而且很痛。扭伤是韧带被拉伤或撕裂，韧带是连接骨与骨的带子，通常没有畸形。拉伤是肌肉或肌腱受伤。两条安全规则：骨折附近只要有伤口，就算看不到骨头也按开放性骨折处理，因为骨端可能刺出来又缩回去了。还有，你的手排除不了骨折，所以脱位或严重扭伤都当作合并骨折来处理。

slides.q: A driver hit his knee on the dashboard in a head-on crash. He is alert and complains only of knee pain. What else must you check carefully?
options: His wrists, for a fall on an outstretched hand
The hip on the same side, for a dislocation or fracture
Nothing else: the knee is clearly the only injury
The opposite ankle, for a twisting injury
slides.say: Time for a question. A driver hit his knee on the dashboard in a head-on crash. He's alert and complains only of knee pain. What else must you check carefully? A, his wrists, for a fall on an outstretched hand. B, the hip on the same side, for a dislocation or fracture. C, nothing else, because the knee is clearly the only injury. D, the opposite ankle, for a twisting injury. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来考考你。一位司机在正面碰撞中膝盖撞到仪表盘，他神志清楚，只说膝盖痛。你还必须仔细检查哪里？A 双手腕，看有没有伸手撑地伤；B 同侧髋部，看有没有脱位或骨折；C 不用查别处，膝盖显然是唯一的伤；D 对侧脚踝，看有没有扭伤。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Force from the dashboard travels up the femur and can push the hip out backward, break the femoral neck, or crack the hip socket. Severe knee pain can distract the patient from the hip. A is a different mechanism; he didn't fall on his hands. C is the trap: an obvious injury hides a less obvious one. D has no mechanism behind it.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。仪表盘的撞击力沿股骨向上传导，可以把髋关节往后推脱位、折断股骨颈，或撞裂髋臼。膝盖剧痛会让病人注意不到髋部。A 是另一种机制，他没有用手撑地；C 正是陷阱：明显的伤会掩盖不明显的伤；D 没有相应的受伤机制。

slides.title: The PCP limb exam
slides.body:
• Compare with the other side: length, angle, rotation, colour
  • Look at and feel the joint above and below
  • Point tenderness is your best sign; never try to cause crepitus
  • Using the limb does not rule out a fracture
CirculationPulselessness, Pallorchild: slow cap refill
NervesParalysis, Paraesthesiaweakness, tingling
TissuePain, Pressuretense, swollen limb
slides.say: Now the exam. Always compare the injured limb with the other side: length, angle, rotation and colour. Look at and feel the joint above and below the injury, because force travels. Point tenderness, meaning pain at one exact spot when you press, is your best sign of a fracture. Don't try to make the bone ends grind; that grating, called crepitus, only adds pain and damage. Then run the six Ps: pain, paralysis, paraesthesia, which means numbness or tingling, pulselessness, pallor, and pressure. In children, a slow capillary refill counts as pallor. And a patient who can still move the limb may still have a fracture.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲检查。一定要和对侧比较：长度、角度、旋转和颜色。检查并触摸受伤处上、下两个关节，因为力会传导。点压痛，就是按到某一个确定的点时疼，是骨折最好的征象。不要故意去制造骨端摩擦，那种粗糙的摩擦感叫骨擦感，只会增加疼痛和损伤。然后逐项查 6P：疼痛、瘫痪、感觉异常（也就是麻木或刺痛）、无脉、苍白和压力。儿童毛细血管再充盈变慢也算苍白。还有，病人还能活动这个肢体，照样可能有骨折。

slides.title: Nerve checks in one minute
slides.body:
NerveMoveFeel
Radialthumbs upback of the thumb web
Median"OK" signtips of thumb, index, middle
Ulnarspread the fingerstip of the little finger
Axillary—outer shoulder (deltoid)
Tibialpoint the toes downsole of the toes
Peronealpull the foot upweb of the 1st and 2nd toes

Document normal findings too, before and after splinting.
slides.say: Here's a nerve check that takes about one minute. In the hand, thumbs up tests the radial nerve, an OK sign tests the median nerve, and spreading the fingers tests the ulnar nerve. For feeling, touch the back of the thumb web for radial, the tips of the thumb, index and middle fingers for median, and the little finger for ulnar. Touch the outer shoulder for the axillary nerve, which a shoulder dislocation can injure. In the foot, pointing the toes down tests the tibial nerve, and pulling the foot up tests the peroneal nerve. As a PCP, document normal findings too, before and after you splint, so the hospital can see any change.
slides.sayZh: 这是一个大约一分钟的神经检查。手部：竖大拇指测桡神经，做 OK 手势测正中神经，张开手指测尺神经。感觉方面：轻触拇指虎口背侧测桡神经，拇指、示指、中指指尖测正中神经，小指测尺神经。轻触肩外侧测腋神经，肩关节脱位可能伤到它。足部：脚尖往下踩测胫神经，把脚往上勾测腓神经。作为 PCP，正常结果也要记录，夹板前后都要记，这样医院才能看出变化。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC musculoskeletal protocol
slides.body:
BC Musculoskeletal Injuries protocol (fractures, dislocations, severe sprains). It has no PCP-only section.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Expose, examine, control major bleeding
  • Stabilize limbs, pelvis or hip; bind the pelvis if appropriate
  • Check distal pulses; realign deformed or pulseless limbs
  • Cold; analgesia before moving stable patients
  • Traction if appropriate; immobilize joints above and below

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry (PCP only), incl. musculoskeletal
  • Shock → Hypovolemia protocol en route: IV, 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Consider TXA for shock from blood loss or hidden bleeding
  • IV acetaminophen (≥ 50 kg: 1,000 mg over 15 min)
slides.say: This is the BC Musculoskeletal Injuries protocol, for suspected fractures, dislocations and severe sprains. Notice that it has no PCP-only section. Everything on the left, from bleeding control and stabilizing the limb, pelvis or hip, to realigning a pulseless limb, cold, traction and pain relief before moving a stable patient, is done at every licence level. So where's the PCP difference? First, your assessment: the functional enquiry is PCP-only, and the musculoskeletal system is one of its nine systems. Second, when fractures bleed enough to cause shock, the hypovolemia protocol gives you an IV, a fluid bolus and TXA, en route. And once you have an IV, acetaminophen can also go in the vein.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的肌肉骨骼损伤流程，适用于疑似骨折、脱位和严重扭伤。注意，它没有 PCP 专属部分。左栏的所有内容，从控制出血、固定肢体、骨盆或髋部，到给无脉肢体复位对线、冷敷、牵引，以及搬动稳定病人前先镇痛，各级别都做。那 PCP 的区别在哪？第一，评估：系统问诊（functional enquiry）只有 PCP 做，肌肉骨骼系统是其中九个系统之一。第二，骨折出血到休克时，低血容量流程给你静脉通路、补液和 TXA，在转运途中做。而且有了静脉通路，对乙酰氨基酚也可以静脉给。

slides.title: Pain relief: same drugs, sharper choices
slides.body:
BC drug (EMR + PCP)Key stops
Entonoxpneumothorax, altered LOC, nitro in the last 5 min
Methoxyflurane 3 mLunder 18, head injury, kidney disease, pregnancy
Acetaminophen 500–1,000 mg POliver disease; a dose in the last 4 h
Ibuprofen 300–400 mg POanticoagulants, GI bleeding, pregnancy

Acetaminophen + ibuprofen may be used together. No opioids in BC EMR/PCP scope.
slides.say: BC says to give analgesia before you move a stable patient, because a splint is easier to tolerate once the pain is down. Note that the four BC pain drugs are the same at both licence levels. Entonox, methoxyflurane, acetaminophen and ibuprofen are all EMR and PCP drugs, and opioids like morphine and fentanyl are outside BC EMR and PCP scope. So your PCP difference is judgment. Take a baseline pain score, rule out every contraindication, take vitals before and after, and reassess the pain. Acetaminophen and ibuprofen may be given together. And the book warns against anti-inflammatories like ketorolac with uncontrolled or internal bleeding, so think twice about ibuprofen in a bleeding patient.
slides.sayZh: BC 要求在搬动稳定病人之前先镇痛，因为疼痛降下来，病人才更能忍受夹板固定。注意：BC 的四种镇痛药在两个级别是一样的。Entonox、甲氧氟烷、对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬都是 EMR 和 PCP 共用的药，吗啡、芬太尼这类阿片类不在 BC EMR/PCP 范围内。所以 PCP 的区别在于判断：先取基线疼痛评分，逐项排除禁忌，给药前后测生命体征，再复评疼痛。对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬可以同时使用。书里还提醒，出血未控制或有内出血时不要用酮咯酸这类抗炎药，所以出血病人用布洛芬要三思。

slides.q: A motorcyclist has a closed mid-shaft femur fracture. He is alert and stable, but has right chest pain and decreased breath sounds on that side. Which pain relief should you avoid?
options: Cold packs and a well-padded splint
slides.say: Here's a PCP drug decision. A motorcyclist has a closed mid-shaft femur fracture. He's alert and stable, but he has right-sided chest pain and decreased breath sounds on that side. Which pain relief should you avoid? A, Entonox. B, methoxyflurane, three millilitres by inhaler. C, acetaminophen, one thousand milligrams by mouth. D, cold packs and a well-padded splint. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 用药决策题。一位摩托车手股骨中段闭合性骨折，神志清楚、生命体征稳定，但右侧胸痛，右侧呼吸音减弱。哪种镇痛方法应该避免？A Entonox；B 甲氧氟烷三毫升经吸入器；C 口服对乙酰氨基酚一千毫克；D 冷敷加衬垫良好的夹板。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A, Entonox. Chest pain with decreased breath sounds after a crash suggests a pneumothorax, and pneumothorax is a listed Entonox contraindication; the gas can move into the trapped air and enlarge it. Methoxyflurane suits an alert, stable adult with no head injury. Acetaminophen by mouth is fine with no liver disease and no dose in the last four hours. Cold and splinting are always good non-drug pain control.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A，Entonox。车祸后胸痛加呼吸音减弱提示气胸，而气胸是 Entonox 明列的禁忌：这种气体会进入被困住的空气里，让气胸变大。甲氧氟烷适合神志清楚、稳定、没有头部外伤的成人；口服对乙酰氨基酚，只要没有肝病、四小时内没服过就可以；冷敷和夹板永远是很好的非药物镇痛。

slides.title: Splinting decisions at PCP level
slides.body:
• Pain relief first; check PMS before and after
  • Fracture: bone ends + the joints above and below
  • Dislocation: the whole bone above and below
  • Badly angulated long bone: gentle in-line traction; stop if pain rises
  • Joint injuries: splint as found, unless circulation is lost
  • Life threat: package the whole patient and go

BC: pulseless limb → one realignment attempt. Pulse returns → stable; still pulseless → unstable.
slides.say: Now the splinting decisions. Give pain relief first; it helps the patient hold still. For a fracture, immobilize the bone ends and the joints above and below. For a dislocation, immobilize the whole bone above and the whole bone below. If a long bone is badly angulated, gentle in-line traction can bring it toward normal, but stop if pain or resistance increases. Joint injuries stay in the position found unless circulation below is lost. BC gives you a clear rule: for a pulseless limb, make one attempt to realign it. If the pulse returns, treat the patient as stable; if not, manage them as unstable. And with a life threat, package the whole patient and go.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲夹板的决策。先镇痛，病人才能保持不动。骨折要固定断端以及上、下两个关节；脱位要固定上、下两整根骨。长骨严重成角，可以用轻柔的纵向牵引把它拉向正常位置，但疼痛或阻力加重就停。关节伤按发现时的位置固定，除非远端没了循环。BC 有一条清楚的规定：肢体无脉时，可以尝试一次复位对线；脉搏恢复，病人按稳定处理；仍然无脉，按不稳定处理。有致命伤时，整体固定病人后马上走。

slides.title: Traction splint: BC STAPLES
slides.body:
BC: suspected mid-shaft femur fracture in a stable patient. Book: not with a pelvic fracture, or another fracture at or below the knee on that leg.

  • Size: beside the injured leg
  • Thigh strap, then Ankle harness above the malleoli
  • Padding
  • Lbs: 10% of body weight, max 15 lb (7 kg); open: max 5 lb
  • Elevate the end; Straps: three, legs strapped together

Once applied, never release traction. Recheck it with every move and every set of vitals.
slides.say: Now the BC traction splint. Use it for a suspected mid-shaft femur fracture in a stable patient. The book adds two contraindications: a suspected pelvic fracture, or another fracture at or below the knee on that leg. Why does traction help? It stops the thigh muscles from pulling the bone ends over each other, and a thigh pulled to length holds less blood than a swollen, round one. Follow STAPLES: size, thigh strap, ankle harness, padding, then pounds: ten percent of body weight, up to fifteen pounds, or seven kilograms, and only five pounds for an open fracture. Elevate and strap. Never release it.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 BC 的牵引夹板。适用于稳定病人的疑似股骨中段骨折。书里还加了两条禁忌：疑似骨盆骨折，或同侧腿膝部及以下另有骨折。牵引为什么有用？它阻止大腿肌肉把骨折两端拉得重叠，而且拉回原长的大腿，比肿成球形的大腿能积的血少。按 STAPLES：量尺寸、系大腿带、踝带、衬垫，然后是磅数：体重的百分之十，最多十五磅，也就是七公斤；开放性骨折最多五磅。再抬高末端、系好绑带。牵引一旦上了就绝不能松开。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A dramatic limb can hide shock: add up the hidden blood loss
  • IV, fluid and TXA go en route; never hold the scene for an IV
  • Acetaminophen: max 4,000 mg/day, all sources (2,000 with liver risk)
  • Methoxyflurane: repeat only after 20 min; max 6 mL in total
  • Vitals and a pain score before and after every drug
  • Air splints expand as they warm up: recheck distal pulses
slides.say: Now the watch-outs that are new at your level. First, a dramatic limb injury can hide shock, so add up the possible blood loss. If the hypovolemia protocol applies, your IV, fluid and TXA happen en route, never as a reason to stay on scene. Second, the drug arithmetic is now yours. For acetaminophen, count every source, including pills taken at home; the daily maximum is four thousand milligrams, or two thousand with liver disease, heavy drinking or malnutrition. Methoxyflurane is repeated only after twenty minutes, six millilitres in total. Take vitals and a pain score before and after every drug. And an air splint put on in the cold expands as the ambulance warms up.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲你这个级别新增的注意事项。第一，吓人的肢体伤可能掩盖休克，所以要把可能的失血量加起来。如果符合低血容量流程，静脉通路、补液和 TXA 都在转运途中做，绝不能成为留在现场的理由。第二，药物计算现在归你管。对乙酰氨基酚要把所有来源都算上，包括病人在家吃的药；每日上限四千毫克，有肝病、重度饮酒或营养不良者降为两千毫克。甲氧氟烷二十分钟后才能重复，总量六毫升。每次给药前后都测生命体征和疼痛评分。还有，在寒冷中上的充气夹板，进入暖和的救护车后会膨胀。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: fentanyl, morphine, ketamine, ketorolac → not in BC EMR/PCP scope
  • Book: "gentle traction" → BC: 10% of body weight, max 15 lb
  • Open femur fracture: max 5 lb of traction
  • Book: SAMPLE, OPQRST → BC: OPQRRRST and LOTARP
  • EMRs have no IV; the PCP starts one when a protocol calls for it
slides.say: Let's line up the book and BC. The book lists fentanyl, morphine, ketamine and ketorolac for fracture pain. None of them are in BC EMR or PCP scope; your options are the four BC drugs. The book only says to apply gentle traction until the limb is aligned. BC gives a number: ten percent of body weight, up to fifteen pounds, and no more than five pounds for an open fracture. For history, the book uses SAMPLE and OPQRST, but BC scoring uses OPQRRRST and LOTARP. And the book places IVs freely, while in BC, EMRs have no IV access, and the PCP starts one when a protocol calls for it.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 对照一下。书里骨折镇痛列了芬太尼、吗啡、氯胺酮和酮咯酸，这些都不在 BC EMR/PCP 范围内，你能用的是 BC 的四种药。书里只说用轻柔牵引直到肢体对线；BC 给了具体数字：体重的百分之十，最多十五磅，开放性骨折不超过五磅。病史方面，书用 SAMPLE 和 OPQRST，BC 评分用 OPQRRRST 和 LOTARP。还有，书里常常开静脉，而在 BC，EMR 没有静脉通路权限，PCP 在流程要求时才开。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Primary survey first; the pelvis and femur can hide litres of blood
  2. Compare sides, joints above and below, the 6 Ps; PMS before and after
  3. Same pain drugs at both levels; traction 10%, max 15 lb (open 5 lb)

Next: pelvis, hip and femur injuries, dislocations, and complications
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: primary survey first, and remember that the pelvis and femur can hide litres of blood. Two: your limb exam compares both sides, checks the joints above and below, runs the six Ps, and documents pulse, movement and sensation before and after the splint. Three: the four BC pain drugs are the same at both levels, so your edge as a PCP is judgment; and BC traction is ten percent of body weight, up to fifteen pounds, or five for an open fracture. Next lesson: the pelvis, hip and femur, the big dislocations, and complications that appear later. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，先做初检，记住骨盆和股骨可以藏好几升血。二，肢体检查要两侧对比、查上下关节、逐项查 6P，夹板前后都记录脉搏、运动和感觉。三，BC 四种镇痛药两个级别一样，所以 PCP 的优势在判断；BC 牵引力是体重的百分之十，最多十五磅，开放性骨折五磅。下节课讲骨盆、髋和股骨、几种重要脱位，以及之后才出现的并发症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
